title: Initiative Chronicle for SLI confidence and dynamic error-budget allocations
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Cross-team initiatives to protect SLOs are hard to track at the level of confidence and remaining error budget. Current trackers show burn rate and simple budgets but don't surface which initiatives should be throttled, accelerated, or reallocated when error budgets deplete. This causes ad hoc triage, delayed rollbacks, and uneven prioritization across platform, runtime, and customer-facing teams.

Proposed solution: Build an "Initiative Chronicle" view and backend service that synthesizes SLIs, error-budget tranches, initiative-level commitments, and a confidence score per initiative. The Chronicle will: (1) ingest SLI time series and current burn rates, (2) map initiatives -> SLOs -> owning teams, (3) compute a confidence index (statistical stability + recent regressions + rollback risk), and (4) expose recommended allocation actions (reduce cadence, freeze rollout, escalate). The product surface includes a console dashboard row for each initiative and an API for automated gating (A/B/canary throttles).

Scope: MVP focuses on HTTP/serving and runtime token-generation SLOs used by Dedicated customers, with pluggable adapters for other SLOs later. The Chronicle uses existing telemetry (SLI aggregator) and integrates with release rollouts and the initiative ledger used by PMs.

Why now: We observed three incidents in last 8 weeks where downstream teams continued canaries despite visible SLO degradation. Automating recommendation and surfacing initiative confidence will speed decisions, reduce manual paging, and make error-budget policy enforcement auditable.
comments: 2025-03-26: Scoping sync with SRE, Runtime, and Console PMs. Agreement on core metrics and ownership boundaries. Action: ENG to prototype confidence score algorithm (assigned ENG-48290).

2025-03-31: Initial data exploration: SLI series available for 90d, but sampling is coarse for token-generation latency. Follow-up: telemetry infra to increase resolution for critical SLOs (dependency created: ENG-50214).
2025-04-03: Design review with Console UX. Agreed to show three-tier confidence badges (High / Medium / Low) plus numeric confidence and next-action suggestions. Figma mock uploaded (link in links).

2025-04-07: Prototype algorithm run completed on historical incidents. Confidence score flagged the problematic initiatives 48-72h earlier than existing alerts in 2/3 test cases. Good initial signal-to-noise.
2025-04-10: PM review: prioritize integrations with rollout service for automated canary pause. Blocking dependency: rollout API needs minor authorization work (ENG-51630).
acceptance_criteria: Console: Chronicle list shows initiative -> primary SLOs -> confidence badge and numeric score for all initiatives in the pilot cohort.
Backend: Confidence service ingests SLI time series and computes score every 10 minutes for pilot SLOs.
Policy: Chronicle recommendations surface at least three suggested actions and include a one-click link to pause or rollback canaries in the rollout service (manual approval required).
Telemetry: Data freshness guarantees documented (max 15m staleness) and monitored; historical retention for audit is available for 90d.
Experiment: In pilot, Chronicle recommendations correlate with manual SRE decisions in >=80% of incidents within the 6-week evaluation window.
success_metrics: Reduce mean time to decision (MTTDecision) for SLO degradations from detection to action by 30% in pilot teams.
Decrease number of cross-team P1 escalations tied to rollout decisions by 25% over 3 months after GA.
Achieve precision >= 0.7 for recommended 'pause rollout' actions in post-hoc validation on prior incidents.
Adoption: 3 internal product/platform teams actively use Chronicle suggestions in first 8 weeks.
risks: False positives: Over-eager recommendations may cause unnecessary rollbacks and slow feature delivery.
Telemetry gaps: Low-resolution SLIs can reduce confidence score fidelity; depends on ENG telemetry work (ENG-50214).
Authorization surface: Integrating with rollout control requires careful RBAC to avoid accidental automated pauses.
User trust: PMs and platform leads may ignore suggested actions unless we provide context and historical rationale.
